scope: Theorem 5.1 (Closedness of the positive-density part) of the manuscript “Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds” (preprints/Taming-implies-compatibility-on-four-manifolds-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 342 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cbddc627efab3dd4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 10-11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a smooth almost complex structure J and a J-Hermitian metric on a closed four-manifold. Suppose that P(α) = Z C αx(ℓ) dλ(x, ℓ) 10 for a finite positive measure λ, with projection µ. Suppose also that Q ∈ L2 is anti-invariant and that P + Q is a closed current. Assume the estimates µ(Br(x)) ≤ Cr2 , (5.1) ZZ dg(x,y)<r |ℓ − τyxm|2 dλ(x, ℓ) dλ(y, m) ≤ Cr4 (5.2) for all sufficiently small r, uniformly in x. Then the limit θ(x) = lim r↓0 r−2 µ(Br(x)) exists at every point. If E = {x : θ(x) > 0}, the current PE = 1EP is closed.
